gen-dafont-quantum-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans reads with big, generous lowercase eyes and strokes like bent copper pipe, a body that never feels cramped by Quantum above it. Nudge its size up a notch if the page feels tight.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans reads like it was drawn with a ruler, its x-height filling the line and its curves left wide open at the ends. Vend Sans keeps that steady, unfussy feel going down a full page, while Quantum above it stays loose and spaced out.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi opens with an e whose eye faces clearly to the right, and its lowercase runs big for its size. Quantum does its best work as a loose, compass-pencil display line; Yaldevi does its best as the quiet sans underneath.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-abeezee: Redux enters every curved letter with a big, visible lead-in, and its wide spacing gives each heading room to stretch out. ABeeZee follows with a ballpoint's pressure-free line, terminals stopping well clear of the stem.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-aldrich: Redux has a mild stress in its o and e that gives the heading a faint hand-turned touch, and Aldrich takes over with a flat, unmodulated line. Its x-height sits close to the cap height, so the plain sans looks cupped and compact beneath.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-alexandria: Redux spaces its letters wide and lets each curve swing in with a visible entrance, with only a modest, smooth weight gradient. And Alexandria is the right foil, a tall-bodied sans with short stems and a wide open c.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-amiko: Contemporary is the first word for Redux, with wide spacing and bowls that shift gently in weight. Amiko brings lowercase strokes as tall as a crayon mark, terminals pointing outward like tongs, under the heading.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-anek-bangla: Anek Bangla brings wide s curves that barely curl in. Beneath Redux, whose thin strokes sit beside moderately weighty stems, the plain sans carries a longer stretch of text with short, friendly reach from midline to ascender.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari has distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone, which makes the plain sans easy to sink into. Redux does its best work up top, with slight but noticeable stroke contrast, while Anek Devanagari holds the text.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati reads big and friendly, its lowercase nearly rivaling the capitals and its c gaping open. Anek Gujarati is what gives this pair its strongest quality, a plain sans that feels generous next to Redux's nib-drawn lines.
